[ ] documentation updated after verified behavior, not before. current evidence apps and future system already received a major route local mobile first pass. social hub already owns a large import based local css system and modular js architecture; its remaining debt is html density, mobile disclosure, consistency, and runtime/browser proof rather than absence of modularity. root geelooy contains dozens of route families; blanket global css is explicitly rejected. procedural core enhancement remains a parallel mission with staged rock/texture/botany/grass architecture awaiting reliable native source promotion. next action audit social hub local style modules for selector scope, overflow, z index, and interaction state gaps; then rewrite only proven weak modules and simplify dense shell markup without changing required dom ids or js contracts.

title: Phase One — Limitless UI Universe
excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Phase One — Limitless UI Universe The Awtsmoos is beyond interface and user flow; Awtsmoos.com can nevertheless reveal one coherent digital world where every route feels related without one route leaking style into another. Ideal experience Every page opens in a calm primary state with o
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — limitless ui universe the awtsmoos is beyond interface and user flow; awtsmoos.com can nevertheless reveal one coherent digital world where every route feels related without one route leaking style into another. ideal experience every page opens in a calm primary state with only the actions needed now. advanced controls live inside native or accessible disclosures, side sheets, command palettes, inspector drawers, contextual rails, or expandable cards. the same conceptual patterns repeat across routes: command/search, identity, status, primary action, contextual details, advanced expansion. mobile is the foundation rather than a compressed desktop afterthought. every route defines its own local color/accent variables beneath an explicit body route selector. shared visual contracts are opt in utilities whose selectors always require a route root or dedicated component root. all panels use min inline size: 0, bounded media, safe wrapping, and explicit scroll ownership. sticky/fixed navigation is sparse, safe area aware, and never hides page content. layering uses semantic local tokens such as content, sticky, overlay, sheet, toast, and modal rather than arbitrary numbers. motion communicates state: hover lift, press compression, disclosure expansion, loading shimmer, focus illumination, route transitions, and success/error feedback. motion automatically collapses under reduced motion preferences. dense creation tools expose a simple primary canvas first; secondary inspectors retract. data heavy admin pages expose summary cards first, filters second, raw payload/advanced controls only on demand. docs show five line quick starts before schemas and failure contracts. social pages foreground conversation/content and retract governance/debug metadata. drive/editor pages foreground the selected file/document and collapse secondary navigation on narrow screens. auth pages remain exceptionally simple and distraction free. every page can survive 320px viewport width without accidental horizontal page scrolling. every interactive element has discoverable keyboard focus and a pressed/active response. any intentional horizontally scrollable region advertises that behavior visually and keeps the document itself fixed. javascript/api universe route boot files become small assemblies that compose domain classes instead of owning logic. dom reads/writes live in views; business state lives in models/policies; network access lives in gateways; orchestration lives in coordinators. public apis accept small serializable option objects and return stable result records. existing low level apis remain available through adapters while ergonomic facades become easier. event names and dom selectors become data registries rather than repeated string literals. abortsignal, timeout, retry, loading, empty, failure, and optimistic states are explicit. complex route state can serialize enough information to reproduce bugs. tests verify public contracts and dom integration separately. documentation universe each route family has a compact readme: purpose, entry point, style root, js assembly, api boundaries, tests, known extensions. architecture docs explain why modules exist and which direction dependencies flow. ui docs define the route's body/root contract and layering/overflow ownership. advanced implementation details stay below quick start guidance.

title: Phase Two — Realistic Route Architecture

headings.text: 3. Route-family migration instead of page-by-page duplication

excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Phase Two — Realistic Route Architecture Chesed imagines one shining universe; Gevurah protects the boundaries. The Awtsmoos is beyond both, while Awtsmoos.com needs an architecture where shared language never becomes shared leakage. Chosen architecture 1. Route owned style manifests Eac
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — realistic route architecture chesed imagines one shining universe; gevurah protects the boundaries. the awtsmoos is beyond both, while awtsmoos.com needs an architecture where shared language never becomes shared leakage. chosen architecture 1. route owned style manifests each production route owns a local style.css or equivalent manifest. the manifest imports small modules. ordinary selectors inside those modules must begin from the route's body/root contract. 2. opt in shared future contracts shared future system modules remain legal only when selectors require explicit route participation such as body[data future page] or a dedicated component root. no :root, naked body, universal interactive selector, or generic .button is allowed in shared route styling. 3. route family migration instead of page by page duplication families with common runtime/dom structures migrate together: social, authoring, heichel reading, account/auth, admin/tooling, media, games. shared components may own styles, but page documents still opt into them explicitly. 4. native disclosure first use for advanced static controls where possible. custom sheets/drawers only where state/navigation requires them. this reduces javascript and improves accessibility. 5. semantic layer tokens each route defines bounded layer variables. shared components may map to them but must not introduce arbitrary global stacking values. 6. javascript boundaries view: dom rendering and accessibility state. policy/model: pure state and validation. gateway: http/storage/browser capability. coordinator/runtime: lifecycle and event orchestration. assembly: dependency wiring only. inheritance is used only when a stable base contract has genuine specializations; composition remains preferred otherwise. first route family wave social hub preserve all existing ids and import map js contracts. split dense html sections into readable multiline markup without changing semantics. audit future hygiene, future interaction baseline, mobile, desktop retraction, interaction disclosure, surface contract. add or correct local overflow/layer/focus states only where absent. verify mobile dock/sheets do not cover content. home audit geelooy/index.css for naked selectors and localize under home route body. preserve launcher/search behavior. verify mobile dock and card grid overflow. docs preserve docs information architecture. simplify first screen to search/navigation/current topic; retract implementation heavy controls. localize any document global selectors. drive preserve existing file operations. collapse secondary panes on narrow screens. make pane ownership/scrolling explicit. verify selection, drag/drop, context menus, dialogs, and keyboard focus. second wave authoring + heichel + profile/social + auth/account. third wave admin/tooling + ai/utilities + media + informational/legal. parallel procedural wave procedural core source promotion proceeds independently but follows the same contracts: simple facade, small focused authorities, whole file rewrites, compatibility tests, documentation after verification.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase three — thirty improvements after critique the awtsmoos renews the plan as surely as the page; awtsmoos.com must challenge its own elegance before asking users to trust it. 1. do not migrate archive/test pages merely to improve counts. 2. identify actual entry routes before touching a family. 3. never add future system imports where a route already owns equivalent local systems. 4. prefer deleting redundant style responsibility over adding another override. 5. audit selectors for accidental shared class collisions before changing markup. 6. preserve every dom id consumed by javascript unless callers are migrated in the same verified wave. 7. prefer min inline size: 0 at layout boundaries over scattered overflow hacks. 8. use overflow wrap: anywhere only for genuinely untrusted identifiers/text. 9. do not hide overflow to conceal layout defects. 10. keep sticky elements inside predictable scroll containers. 11. treat mobile safe area insets as route shell responsibilities. 12. verify keyboard reachability after adding retractable panels. 13. ensure native summaries have hover, active, focus visible, and open states. 14. ensure form controls have invalid/disabled/read only styles where relevant. 15. avoid hover only affordances on touch first surfaces. 16. add active state feedback even for links styled as cards/buttons. 17. avoid animation on layout heavy properties when transform/opacity can communicate the same state. 18. keep reduced motion output functionally equivalent. 19. use content visibility only on long independent lists, not interactive regions requiring immediate measurement. 20. keep z index token ranges small and documented. 21. browser check focus rings against actual backgrounds. 22. browser check 320px, 375px, tablet, and desktop widths. 23. measure document scrollwidth after every shell rewrite. 24. check console and failed network resources after each route family wave. 25. run route specific tests before broad repository suites. 26. read back every rewritten file in full. 27. compare planned vs actual files and record delta. 28. update readme/architecture only after implementation proof. 29. keep procedural world ui demos under the same local style contract. 30. treat any newly discovered global selector or oversized source file as remaining work rather than silently accepting debt.
